lesson.title: Agreement Drills
lesson.subtitle: allée, allés, allées: why participles wear gender and plural agreements only inside the être house.

hook.title: Participle Agreement Inside the être House
hook.content: Inside the être house, the past participle agrees with the subject in gender (-e) and number (-s): il est allé, elle est allée (+e), ils sont allés (+s), elles sont allées (+es)!

footnotes.title: Why allé, allée, allés, allées sound 100% identical (/ale/)
footnotes.content: Adding -e or -s to allé, arrivé, parti, venu changes NOTHING in pronunciation — only your pen adds the agreement badge!

pattern.title: Same Sound in the Mouth, Gender/Number Badge on the Page
pattern.content: Add -e for a female subject and -s for a plural subject on être-house participles, while keeping avoir participles un-agreed with the subject.
pattern.linguist_note: Subject-participle agreement with être reflects the copular origin of the construction.
pattern.trap_note: Never add subject agreement to an avoir participle (*Elle a mangée is wrong!) — subject agreement belongs ONLY to the être house!

exercises.prompt: Match each subject with the correctly agreed written form of 'went' (allé):
exercises.target_answer: allé, allée (+e), allés (+s), allées (+es), mangé (NO agreement with subject!)
exercises.meaning: Il est... (one man), Elle est... (one woman), Nous sommes... (men or mixed group), Elles sont... (group of women), Elle a... (with avoir: 'she ate')
exercises.explanation: Only être-house participles agree with the subject!

exercises.prompt: Compare 'She went to the café' (être) vs. 'She ate at the café' (avoir). Which written pair is right?
options: Elle est allé au café / Elle a mangé au café
Elle est allée au café / Elle a mangé au café
Elle est allée au café / Elle a mangée au café
exercises.target_answer: Elle est allée au café / Elle a mangé au café
exercises.meaning: être agrees with Elle (allée); avoir does NOT agree with Elle (mangé)!
exercises.explanation: Subject agreement happens inside the être house (allée), never on avoir participles (mangé).

exercises.prompt: Write 'She left this morning' (Elle + est + parti with feminine agreement + ce matin):
exercises.explanation: parti adds feminine -e to agree with Elle: Elle est partie.

exercises.idea: Marie arrived yesterday and she stayed at my place
cues: Marie arrived yesterday → Marie est arrivée hier
and she stayed at my place → et elle est restée chez moi
idea_parts: first clause → Marie est arrivée hier
second clause → et elle est restée chez moi
exercises.target_answer: Marie est arrivée hier et elle est restée chez moi
exercises.meaning: Marie arrived yesterday and stayed at my place
exercises.explanation: Both arrivée and restée add -e to agree with Marie / elle.

diagnosis.cue: Add feminine -e to both être participles for Marie: arrivée, restée.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Elles sont venues avec nous hier soir
exercises.target_answer: Elles sont venues avec nous hier soir
exercises.meaning: They (f.) came with us last night
exercises.explanation: venues carries both feminine -e and plural -s for Elles.
exercises.affirmation: You wrote venues with -es for Elles!

summary.outcome: Write accurate gender and number agreements (-e, -s, -es) on être-house participles.

use_example.german: Elle est sortie, mais elle a oublié son parapluie.
use_example.english: She went out, but she forgot her umbrella.

summary.takeaway: être participles agree with the subject (Elle est allée); avoir participles do not (Elle a mangé).
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([19] The Storytelling Past): see how Agreement Drills leads directly into The Storytelling Past.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "Marie arrived yesterday and stayed at my place" in French:
twist.target_answer: Marie est arrivée hier et elle est restée chez moi
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Marie est arrivée hier et elle est restée chez moi" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Agreement Drills.

allé.etymology_derivation: aller's participle; motion verbs form their past with être — and the participle agrees: allée, allés, allées.

arrivé.etymology_derivation: Late Latin ad rīpam 'to the shore' — to arrive was to land on a riverbank.

venu.etymology_derivation: Latin venīre — venue (where you come), venture, adventure (what you come to).

parti.etymology_derivation: partir takes être in the past: je suis parti(e).

sorti.context_phrase: Elle est sortie avec ses amis.
sorti.context_translation: She went out with her friends.
sorti.etymology_derivation: sortir takes être in the past.

resté.etymology_derivation: Latin restāre 'to stand back, remain'. Staying counts as motion's family — être-house logic.

être.etymology_derivation: Latin esse 'to be' → essere → être. English kept the root in essence and quintessential — the being-ness inside the word.

suis.etymology_derivation: je suis is literally 'I follow' — Latin sequor, the root of sequence and sequel. Being is following, historically.

nous.etymology_derivation: Latin nōs — English keeps the root in nostrum.

vous.etymology_derivation: Latin vōs 'you all' promoted to politeness — the same T–V ladder as German Sie and English's lost 'ye'.
